claims.assertion: The trip is a metered RydeTAXI fare (charged $57.73, distance $40.96 on 29.1 km, time $11.40 on 43.8 min), so distance actually driven enters the fare at $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.41/km.
The GPS track shows two off-route segments: 18:40–18:45 added 3.17 km and 18:59–19:08 added 4.78 km, a total of 8.5 km / +41% over the 20.6 km optimal route.

The first detour is excused: the driver asked at 18:37 to go round via Kranji Expressway because of traffic, the rider agreed at 18:38, and the rider's consent timestamp precedes the segment's 18:40 start.

The second off-route segment (18:59–19:08, 4.78 km extra) was not consented to: the only chat in the record is the rider's 18:38 agreement to a Kranji Expressway route, which does not cover this later deviation, and the driver admits in his statement he took the 'second turn-off' on his own GPS rerouting.

No reasonable cause is made out for the second segment: the only traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Bukit Timah Expressway and band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Pan Island Expressway, neither being band 1 or 2, and there are no traffic incidents anywhere near the route during the trip window.

The second segment is therefore an unexempted detour, and the rider is owed the metered mileage it added: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74, computed from fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km on the fare fact and the extra_km on the GPS fact.
No surge applied (1.0×) and no waiting fee was charged, so no part of the refund request is inflated by surcharges or add-ons.

weaknesses: The length of the trip hides a large excess: actual 29.0 km vs 20.6 km optimal (+8.5 km, +41%) is inconsistent with a rider who agreed to only one short jam-avoiding detour, but the fare fact F5 bills the whole 8.5 km as $11.96 and the rider asks for only part of it back — the driver will argue the rider's 18:38 blanket 'go ahead' to a route change at the very start of the trip condoned the driver's routing discretion thereafter.

My own client's record is not spotless: F15 shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld (though not route-related), which the driver can use to suggest the rider files opportunistic complaints; the driver's record (F16: 883 trips, 1 dispute, 0 upheld) is cleaner and the driver can also cite F10's assertion that the second turn-off was GPS rerouting, i.e. a machine recommendation rather than a voluntary deviation.

claims.assertion: The trip is a metered RydeTAXI fare (charged $57.73, distance $40.96 on 29.1 km, time $11.40 on 43.8 min), so distance actually driven enters the fare at $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.41/km.
The GPS track shows two off-route segments: 18:40–18:45 added 3.17 km and 18:59–19:08 added 4.78 km, a total of 8.5 km / +41% over the 20.6 km optimal route.

The first detour is excused: the driver asked at 18:37 to go round via Kranji Expressway because of traffic, the rider agreed at 18:38, and the rider's consent timestamp precedes the segment's 18:40 start.

The second off-route segment (18:59–19:08, 4.78 km extra) was not consented to: the only chat in the record is the rider's 18:38 agreement to a Kranji Expressway route, which does not cover this later deviation, and the driver admits in his statement he took the 'second turn-off' on his own GPS rerouting.

No reasonable cause is made out for the second segment: the only traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Bukit Timah Expressway and band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Pan Island Expressway, neither being band 1 or 2, and there are no traffic incidents anywhere near the route during the trip window.

The second segment is therefore an unexempted detour, and the rider is owed the metered mileage it added: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74, computed from fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km on the fare fact and the extra_km on the GPS fact.
No surge applied (1.0×) and no waiting fee was charged, so no part of the refund request is inflated by surcharges or add-ons.

weaknesses: The length of the trip hides a large excess: actual 29.0 km vs 20.6 km optimal (+8.5 km, +41%) is inconsistent with a rider who agreed to only one short jam-avoiding detour, but the fare fact F5 bills the whole 8.5 km as $11.96 and the rider asks for only part of it back — the driver will argue the rider's 18:38 blanket 'go ahead' to a route change at the very start of the trip condoned the driver's routing discretion thereafter.

My own client's record is not spotless: F15 shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld (though not route-related), which the driver can use to suggest the rider files opportunistic complaints; the driver's record (F16: 883 trips, 1 dispute, 0 upheld) is cleaner and the driver can also cite F10's assertion that the second turn-off was GPS rerouting, i.e. a machine recommendation rather than a voluntary deviation.

claims.assertion: The first off-route segment (18:40–18:45, +3.17 km, F3) is exempt because the driver proposed the reroute in the app at 18:37 (F8) and the rider expressly agreed at 18:38 (F9), i.e. before the segment began at 18:40.

Only the second off-route segment (18:59–19:08, extra 4.78 km, F4) is an unexempted deviation: the driver's statement that it was a GPS reroute (F10) is not corroborated by any incident on the optimal route (F13), and no chat message shows the rider agreed to it.

The refund on the unexempted segment is limited to the metered mileage portion: 4.78 extra km × the trip's per-km rate of $1.41 (F5, $11.96 ÷ 8.5 km) = $6.74, per RD-2's RydeTAXI branch which refunds only extra_km × distance rate and excludes map-matching residue.

No fare item beyond the meter needs unwinding: surge is 1.0× (F6), waiting fee is $0.00 and the only added item is the $1.47 published platform fee in the $57.73 total (F7), so no FARE-1 unpublished charge exists.
No account flag is warranted in this case: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the profile (F16), so RD-6's 'repeated' precondition is not met.

weaknesses: The driver's claim that the second deviation was only a GPS reroute rests on his own statement (F10) and is contradicted by the system record: no traffic incident was recorded near the route (F13), and the segment added 4.78 km with the track reaching 1687 m from the optimal route (F4), which the rider can use to show the devi-ation was neither traffic-forced nor consented to.
